findings.title: Email-change flow bypasses the new blocked-email validation
findings.body: `change_email` only checks uniqueness and then creates an `EmailToken` directly; it never assigns the address to the user and runs `User` validation before issuing the token. Consequently, an existing user can request and confirm a blocked address through this endpoint, bypassing `EmailValidator` and the blocked-email policy entirely. Validate the requested address (including the email validator) before creating the token, or enforce the policy in the token-confirmation path as well.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive while signup emails are not normalized
findings.body: The lookup compares the supplied email verbatim, but signup assigns `params[:email]` directly and does not normalize it. A block entry such as `block@spamfromhome.org` can therefore be bypassed by registering `Block@spamfromhome.org` (and potentially other equivalent casing variants). Normalize both stored blocked addresses and lookup input using the application's canonical email normalization (`Email.downcase(...).strip`) and enforce uniqueness on that canonical value.

findings.title: Match statistics are incremented once per validation pass, not once per signup attempt
findings.body: Calling `BlockedEmail.should_block?` from the validator mutates `match_count` and `last_match_at` every time validations run. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` is always called before `user.save`, and `save` validates again, so a single signup submission increments the counter twice (including for `do_nothing` records). Other callers that invoke `valid?` repeatedly have the same effect, making the recorded statistics inaccurate. Record an attempted match once at the request/policy boundary, or make validation side-effect-free.
